definition: a short chain of amino acids linked together, smaller than a protein.

collocations.example: Each peptide bond links two amino acids within the chain.
The signal peptide directs the new protein to its destination.

definition: a single floor or level of a building.

collocations.example: They bought a small two-story house near the station.
Her office is on the top story of the building.

definition: a rubber covering fitted around a wheel to grip the road.

collocations.example: We had to stop and fix a flat tire.
He taught me how to change a tire quickly.

definition: inflammation of the inner lining of the colon.

collocations.example: She was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis last year.
Some patients develop colitis after taking certain antibiotics.

definition: relating to, resembling, or containing a cyst or cysts.

collocations.example: Cystic fibrosis is a serious inherited disease affecting the lungs.
On the ultrasound, the mass appeared cystic rather than solid.

definition: a current of cool air moving through an enclosed space.

collocations.example: I felt a cold draft coming from the open window.
They put a towel down to block the draft under the door.

definition: the practice of selling goods aggressively, especially in the street.

collocations.example: Street hawking is banned in parts of the city center.
He made a living hawking goods from a small cart.

definition: a small area of dead tissue caused by a blocked blood supply.

collocations.example: The scan showed a cerebral infarct in the left hemisphere.
The drug helped to reduce the infarct size after the attack.

definition: a type of white blood cell that helps the body fight infection.

collocations.example: A T lymphocyte attacks cells that are already infected.
The patient's lymphocyte count dropped sharply during the illness.

definition: a young person with closely shaved hair, often linked to an aggressive group.

collocations.example: A skinhead gang caused trouble outside the stadium that night.
The film portrays a neo-Nazi skinhead who later changes his views.

definition: an old literary word meaning two or a pair.

collocations.example: The old oak was split in twain by a bolt of lightning.
They lead separate lives, and never the twain shall meet.

definition: from what place or source; from where.

collocations.example: The ancient vase was returned to the country whence it came.
No one could say from whence the rumor had started.

definition: in which; in what way or respect.

collocations.example: Wherein lies the real difference between the two proposals?
The contract has a clause wherein both parties share the costs.

definition: immediately after which; and then.

collocations.example: He paid the bill whereupon he left the restaurant quietly.
The verdict was read out, whereupon the crowd rose to applaud.

definition: that or those over there; at a distance (old-fashioned or dialect).

collocations.example: A small cottage stands on yon hill across the valley.
You will find the old well over yon, past the barn.

definition: to walk or move about, especially while recovering from illness or surgery.

collocations.example: After weeks of therapy, she could finally ambulate independently again.
Nurses help the patient ambulate soon after the operation.

definition: to release someone from service in the armed forces; to demobilize.

collocations.example: The government began to demob the troops after the war ended.
He was finally demobbed and returned home in 1946.

definition: an old-fashioned form of the verb 'does'.

collocations.example: As the saying goes, the lady doth protest too much.
What doth it profit a man to gain the whole world?

definition: the government department or funds that manage a country's public money.

collocations.example: The Chancellor of the Exchequer announced new taxes this morning.
The failing project became a serious drain on the exchequer.

definition: a narrow inlet of the sea, especially in Scotland; an estuary.

collocations.example: A famous railway bridge crosses the Firth of Forth.
Small fishing boats sail up the firth at high tide.

definition: a place where people are held in custody, especially while awaiting trial.

collocations.example: He was thrown in jail for refusing to pay the fine.
The prisoner spent the night alone in a jail cell.

definition: a person who does not belong to one of the main world religions; a pagan.

collocations.example: Missionaries traveled far to convert the heathen in distant lands.
The ancient tribe worshiped many heathen gods and spirits.

definition: a person who has leprosy.

collocations.example: The missionary doctor chose to treat a leper every day.
The island once held a leper colony in strict isolation.

definition: (informal) a crazy, foolish, or eccentric person.

collocations.example: Everyone thought the inventor was a complete loony at first.
Don't call him a loony just because his ideas sound strange.

definition: a chemical group (CH3) derived from methane and found in many compounds.

collocations.example: The molecule has a methyl group attached to its core.
Methyl alcohol is highly toxic and must not be swallowed.

definition: (informal) a very foolish or stupid person.

collocations.example: I felt like a complete moron after locking my keys inside.
Stop talking so slowly; don't treat me like a moron.

definition: relating to the muscle of the heart.

collocations.example: A myocardial infarction is the medical term for a heart attack.
The test can detect early signs of myocardial damage.

definition: a piece of soft, absorbent material worn by a baby to hold waste.

collocations.example: He learned how to change a diaper before the baby arrived.
Keeping the skin dry helps prevent painful diaper rash.

definition: a woman's or girl's undergarment covering the lower body (usually 'panties').

collocations.example: She keeps a panty liner in her bag just in case.
He bought a pair of panties as part of the gift set.

definition: (informal) trivial or worthless reading matter, ideas, or entertainment.

collocations.example: Critics dismissed the show as mindless pap for the masses.
The network just serves up pap night after night.

definition: a trained specialist who treats injury and disability with exercise and massage.

collocations.example: The doctor advised her to see a physical therapist weekly.
A licensed physical therapist designed his recovery program carefully.

definition: a length of hair divided into three and woven together.

collocations.example: She tied her thick hair into a single long braid.
She likes to wear her hair in a braid at work.

definition: the place or role that someone or something would otherwise have (used in set phrases).

collocations.example: The deputy attended the important meeting in his stead.
These skills will stand you in good stead later in life.

definition: the final stop at the end of a railway or bus route; an end point.

collocations.example: The crowded bus terminus was busy during the morning rush.
The old station was once the terminus of the line.

definition: a small, slender sea fish with white flesh, eaten as food.

collocations.example: The chef served a lightly fried fillet of whiting.
We bought some fresh whiting from the harbor market.

definition: (in the past) a public institution where poor people lived and were made to work.

collocations.example: The orphan was sent to the workhouse at a young age.
Conditions in the parish workhouse were harsh and crowded.

definition: (historical) a man who owned and farmed a small piece of his own land.

collocations.example: His grandfather was a sturdy yeoman with his own land.
Each yeoman farmer held a few acres near the village.
